tasks.title: Select an OB/GYN or midwife
tasks.description: Choose your primary prenatal care provider early — practices often fill up quickly.

tasks.title: Schedule all prenatal appointments
tasks.description: Book out your recurring checkups so you don't scramble to find open slots later.

tasks.title: Complete anatomy scan and key ultrasounds
tasks.description: This detailed scan checks on baby's development and flags anything that needs follow-up.

tasks.title: Select a pediatrician
tasks.description: Your baby will need a pediatrician lined up before their first checkup after birth.

tasks.title: Enroll in a childbirth class
tasks.description: Learn what to expect during labor and delivery so you feel more prepared.

tasks.title: Take a breastfeeding or feeding preparation class
tasks.description: Build feeding confidence before baby arrives, whether you plan to breastfeed or bottle-feed.

tasks.title: Take an infant CPR and first aid class
tasks.description: A hands-on safety class that prepares you to respond to common infant emergencies.

tasks.title: Pre-register at the hospital or birth center
tasks.description: Completing paperwork ahead of time speeds up check-in when labor begins.

tasks.title: Tour the hospital or birth center
tasks.description: Seeing the labor and delivery unit ahead of time helps you know what to expect on the day.

tasks.title: Create a birth plan
tasks.description: Write down your preferences for labor, delivery, and immediate postpartum care.

tasks.title: Receive recommended vaccines — Tdap and flu
tasks.description: These vaccines help protect both you and your baby during pregnancy and after birth.

tasks.title: Research pain management options for labor
tasks.description: Understand your choices ahead of time so you can make informed decisions in the moment.

tasks.title: Research postpartum mental health support
tasks.description: Know the warning signs and resources available in case you need support after birth.

tasks.title: Schedule postpartum follow-up appointments
tasks.description: Book your own recovery checkup along with baby's first pediatrician visit.

tasks.title: Identify a lactation consultant
tasks.description: Having a consultant lined up makes it easier to get help quickly if feeding issues come up.

tasks.title: Set up the crib or bassinet
tasks.description: Get baby's sleep space assembled and safety-checked well before their arrival.

tasks.title: Purchase and set up a baby monitor
tasks.description: Choose a monitor and test it in the nursery so it's ready before baby comes home.

tasks.title: Paint or decorate the nursery
tasks.description: Finish any painting early to allow time for fumes to clear and decor to dry.

tasks.title: Assemble nursery furniture
tasks.description: Put together the dresser, glider, and other furniture pieces ahead of time.

tasks.title: Wash and organize newborn clothing by size
tasks.description: Pre-washing with a gentle detergent and sorting by size saves time in the newborn haze.

tasks.title: Set up a changing station
tasks.description: Stock a dedicated spot with diapers, wipes, and creams within easy reach.

tasks.title: Set up a nursing or feeding station
tasks.description: Create a comfortable spot with water, snacks, and burp cloths for late-night feedings.

tasks.title: Install blackout curtains in the nursery
tasks.description: Help baby (and you) sleep better by keeping the nursery dark for naps and bedtime.

tasks.title: Purchase a white noise machine
tasks.description: Consistent background noise can help soothe baby and mask household sounds.

tasks.title: Baby-proof electrical outlets
tasks.description: Cover exposed outlets in the nursery and common areas before baby starts moving.

tasks.title: Anchor heavy furniture to walls
tasks.description: Secure dressers and shelving units to prevent tip-over hazards.

tasks.title: Deep clean the home before baby arrives
tasks.description: Give the house a thorough clean now — it'll be much harder to find the time later.

tasks.title: Research health insurance options for baby
tasks.description: Understand your plan's requirements and deadlines for adding a new dependent.

tasks.title: Add baby to health insurance within 30 days of birth
tasks.description: Most insurers require enrollment within a strict window after birth — don't miss it.

tasks.title: Create a monthly baby budget
tasks.description: Estimate new recurring costs like diapers, formula, and childcare to plan ahead.

tasks.title: Review and update your will
tasks.description: Make sure guardianship and asset decisions reflect your growing family.

tasks.title: Review and update life insurance coverage
tasks.description: Confirm your coverage is enough to protect your family's new financial needs.

tasks.title: Update beneficiary designations on accounts
tasks.description: Add your child as a beneficiary on retirement accounts and other policies as appropriate.

tasks.title: Research childcare costs and options
tasks.description: Daycare and nanny waitlists can be long — start researching well ahead of your return to work.

tasks.title: Apply for parental or FMLA leave
tasks.description: Submit paperwork early to make sure your leave is approved before your due date.

tasks.title: Open a college savings account (529 plan)
tasks.description: Starting early gives tax-advantaged savings more time to grow.

tasks.title: Research WIC or financial assistance programs
tasks.description: Check eligibility for programs that can help offset costs for formula, food, and more.

tasks.title: Purchase an infant car seat
tasks.description: You'll need this installed before you can be discharged from the hospital.

tasks.title: Have car seat installation inspected by a certified tech
tasks.description: A free inspection confirms the seat is installed correctly before you need it.

tasks.title: Purchase a stroller system
tasks.description: Pick a stroller that fits your lifestyle and, if needed, works with your car seat.

tasks.title: Obtain a breast pump (often covered by insurance)
tasks.description: Check your insurance benefits — many plans cover a pump at no cost.

tasks.title: Stock up on newborn diapers and wipes
tasks.description: Have a solid supply on hand so you're not making a diaper run right after coming home.

tasks.title: Set up a baby swing, bouncer, or rocker
tasks.description: A safe spot to place baby down for a few minutes can be a lifesaver early on.

tasks.title: Purchase a baby carrier or wrap
tasks.description: Babywearing frees up your hands while keeping baby close and comforted.

tasks.title: Purchase a baby bathtub
tasks.description: A supportive infant tub makes bath time safer and easier in the early months.

tasks.title: Buy a diaper bag
tasks.description: Choose a bag with enough storage and organization for outings with baby.

tasks.title: Set up a bottle cleaning station and sterilizer
tasks.description: Have a system ready for washing and sterilizing bottles and pump parts.

tasks.title: Purchase a baby thermometer and nail file kit
tasks.description: Small essentials that come in handy from the very first days home.

tasks.title: Stock a medicine cabinet with baby-safe essentials
tasks.description: Keep infant pain reliever, saline drops, and a nasal aspirator on hand.

tasks.title: Plan postpartum help from family or friends
tasks.description: Line up support in advance so you're not coordinating help in the middle of recovery.

tasks.title: Research and hire a postpartum doula if desired
tasks.description: A postpartum doula can provide hands-on support with newborn care and recovery.

tasks.title: Prepare freezer meals for after the birth
tasks.description: Stock the freezer now so healthy meals are ready when you're too tired to cook.

tasks.title: Set up a meal train with friends and family
tasks.description: Coordinate a schedule so meals keep coming during the first weeks postpartum.

tasks.title: Discuss newborn care responsibilities with partner
tasks.description: Talk through how you'll divide nighttime feedings, diaper changes, and chores.

tasks.title: Discuss feeding approach with partner
tasks.description: Align on your feeding plan so you can support each other once baby arrives.

tasks.title: Prepare other children for the new baby
tasks.description: Help siblings understand what's changing and how they can be involved.

tasks.title: Prepare pets for the new baby's arrival
tasks.description: Gradually introduce new sounds and routines to help pets adjust ahead of time.

tasks.title: Identify your postpartum support network
tasks.description: Know who you can call for emotional support, advice, or a few hours of help.

tasks.title: Talk to your employer about leave logistics
tasks.description: Confirm timing, paperwork, and coverage plans well ahead of your leave.

tasks.title: Pack the hospital bag
tasks.description: Have essentials for you, your partner, and baby packed and ready to grab.

tasks.title: Prepare a go-bag for the birth partner
tasks.description: A separate bag with the birth partner's essentials keeps everyone ready to go.

tasks.title: Organize important documents for the hospital
tasks.description: Gather your ID, insurance card, and birth plan into one easy-to-find folder.

tasks.title: Research newborn screening tests
tasks.description: Understand the standard tests performed shortly after birth so nothing is a surprise.

tasks.title: Research and decide on cord blood banking
tasks.description: Decide whether private or public cord blood banking is right for your family.

tasks.title: Update emergency contacts
tasks.description: Make sure your emergency contact list reflects your current support network.

tasks.title: Plan your birth announcement
tasks.description: Decide how and when you'll share the news with family and friends.
